speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in; your symptoms of right knee swelling combined with a family history suggest a possible genetic joint disorder. To narrow this down, can you tell me if you experience pain or stiffness, and does the swelling come on suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A or B presenting with a hemarthrosis (bleeding into the joint). Given the age, spontaneous swelling after minor activity, and family history, this is highly suggestive of a factor deficiency. Please confirm if there is a family history of excessive bleeding after tooth extraction, circumcision, or minor cuts, and REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII and Factor IX levels.
